description: Add hardened Docker Compose configuration for ChromaDB with authentication, security options (read-only filesystem, no-new-privileges), and localhost-only binding. Also update the main docker-compose.yml if it exists.
steps: Step 1 - Create docker-compose.chroma.yml with the hardened ChromaDB service: chromadb/chroma:latest image, container name chromadb-dms, port 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 (localhost only), volumes for chroma_data and chroma_config, environment variables for token auth provider and persistence, security_opt no-new-privileges, read_only true, tmpfs /tmp:size=100M,mode=1777.
Step 2 - Create a chroma_config/ directory with a placeholder token.txt file (with a generated random token) and a README explaining how to set the auth token.
Step 3 - Update app/core/config.py to add CHROMA_AUTH_TOKEN setting (used to authenticate with ChromaDB when token auth is enabled).
Step 4 - Update app/services/vectordb.py (if it exists) or create it to pass authentication credentials when connecting to ChromaDB (use the token from config).
Step 5 - Add a healthcheck to the docker-compose.chroma.yml service.
Step 6 - Add tests/test_docker_compose.py that validates the docker-compose.chroma.yml file is valid YAML and contains expected security configurations (parse YAML and assert on structure).
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.chroma.yml exists with hardened ChromaDB configuration
read_only and no-new-privileges security options are set
chroma_config directory exists with token placeholder
ChromaDB client in app passes auth token when configured
verification: uv run ruff check app/ tests/
